One says: "so-and-so is in a ʿaṣar" and "in a ʿuṣra" when he is in a fortress that cannot be overcome.

zajjaj:50-50.t:
His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿وَقالَ المَلِكُ ائْتُونِي بِهِ﴾: when he was informed of his standing in knowledge of interpretation, he sought him. ﴿قالَ ارْجِعْ إلى رَبِّكَ فاسْألْهُ﴾, that is: to your master; ”رَبُّ الشَّيْءِ“ (the rabb of a thing) is its owner.
﴿فاسْألْهُ ما بالُ النِّسْوَةِ اللاتِي قَطَّعْنَ أيْدِيَهُنَّ﴾; ”اَللّائِي قَطَّعْنَ“ is also permissible. That is: "ask him to yastaʿmil the soundness of my innocence of what I was accused of".
[Translator's note: «أنْ يَسْتَعْمِلَ» literally means "to make use of"; the context suggests "to ascertain" (perhaps «يَسْتَعْلِمَ»). Translated as written.]
It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: «"Had I been in Yūsuf's place and then the messenger had come to me, I would have hastened to him"». He ﷺ admired Yūsuf's resolve and patience when the king summoned him: he did not hasten to him until he knew that the soundness of his innocence had been established with the king.

zajjaj:51-51.t:
﴿قالَ ما خَطْبُكُنَّ إذْ راوَدْتُنَّ يُوسُفَ﴾: Yūsuf, upon him be peace, did not single out the wife of al-ʿAzīz by name, out of good companionship and courtesy on his part, so he included her among the women.
[Translator's note: The Quranic words here are spoken by the king; the source's remark refers to Yūsuf's earlier request (verse 50) mentioning only «النِّسْوَةِ». Translated as written.]
His saying: ﴿قُلْنَ حاشَ لِلَّهِ ما عَلِمْنا عَلَيْهِ مِن سُوءٍ﴾: it has been read ”حاشَ لِلَّهِ“ and ”حاشا لِلَّهِ“, and al-Ḥasan read ”حاشْ لِلَّهِ“ with sukūn of the shīn. There is no disagreement among the grammarians that the quiescence is not permissible, because combining two quiescent letters is not permissible, nor is it of the speech of the Arabs. ﴿ما عَلِمْنا عَلَيْهِ مِن سُوءٍ﴾: so the women informed the king of Yūsuf's innocence. ﴿قالَتِ امْرَأتُ العَزِيزِ الآنَ حَصْحَصَ الحَقُّ﴾, that is: it has emerged and become clear. Its derivation in the language is from ”اَلْحِصَّةُ“ (share, portion), that is: the share of the truth and its side have become distinct from the side of falsehood.

zajjaj:52-52.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أنِّي لَمْ أخُنْهُ بِالغَيْبِ﴾: this is the saying of Yūsuf, upon him be peace. The meaning is: "I wanted to make clear to the king the matter of his wife and the women, so that he would know that I did not betray him in secret". ”ذَلِكَ“ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or, if you wish, as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ, as if he said: "my affair is that". It is narrated that Jibrīl, upon him be peace, said to him: "Not even when you undid the waistband?" — and it has been said: "Not even when you inclined?" — so he said: ﴿وَما أُبَرِّئُ نَفْسِي إنَّ النَّفْسَ لأمّارَةٌ بِالسُّوءِ إلا ما رَحِمَ رَبِّي﴾ [Yūsuf: 53]. The position of ”ما“ is accusative as an exception (istithnāʾ).

zajjaj:54-54.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أسْتَخْلِصْهُ لِنَفْسِي﴾ is jussive (majzūm), as the answer to the command (jawāb al-amr). The meaning of ”أسْتَخْلِصْهُ“ is: I will make him exclusively mine, no one sharing him with me. ﴿فَلَمّا كَلَّمَهُ قالَ إنَّكَ اليَوْمَ لَدَيْنا مَكِينٌ أمِينٌ﴾, that is: we have come to know your trustworthiness and your innocence of what you were accused of.

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿قالَ اجْعَلْنِي عَلى خَزائِنِ الأرْضِ﴾, that is: over its wealth. ﴿إنِّي حَفِيظٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾, that is: I will guard it and I know the ways of its disposal. He only asked him to put him over the storehouses of the land because the prophets were sent to establish truth and justice and to put things in their proper places; and Yūsuf, upon him be peace, knew that there was no one more upright in that than he, nor better at putting it in its proper places, so he asked for that out of a desire for the common good.

zajjaj:59-59.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَمّا جَهَّزَهم بِجَهازِهِمْ قالَ ائْتُونِي بِأخٍ لَكم مِن أبِيكُمْ﴾: this — and Allah knows best — was preceded by talk that led to what necessitated asking them for their brother, because he would not say "Bring me a brother of yours from your father" without something having occurred that necessitated this saying. So it is as if — and Allah knows best — he asked them about their news, their affairs and their number, and so he ventured to make this request.
﴿ألا تَرَوْنَ أنِّي أُوفِي الكَيْلَ وأنا خَيْرُ المُنْـزِلِينَ﴾: because when he lodged them, he hosted them well.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿فَإنْ لَمْ تَأْتُونِي بِهِ فَلا كَيْلَ لَكم عِنْدِي ولا تَقْرَبُونِ﴾: the reading is with kasra of the nūn, and fatḥa — with fatḥa of the nūn — is permissible, because it is the nūn of the plural, as He said: ﴿فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 54] with fatḥa of the nūn. Then ”وَلا تَقْرَبُونَ“ has the wording of a statement and the meaning of a command.

zajjaj:61-61.t: ﴿قالُوا سَنُراوِدُ عَنْهُ أباهُ وإنّا لَفاعِلُونَ﴾: ”وَإنّا لَفاعِلُونَ“ is emphasis (tawkīd).

zajjaj:62-62.t: ﴿وَقالَ لِفِتْيانِهِ﴾ and ”لِفِتْيَتِهِ“ — both have been read. ”اَلْفِتْيانُ“ and ”اَلْفِتْيَةُ“ are the slaves in this place. ﴿اجْعَلُوا بِضاعَتَهم في رِحالِهِمْ لَعَلَّهم يَعْرِفُونَها إذا انْقَلَبُوا إلى أهْلِهِمْ لَعَلَّهم يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: there are two ways in this. That is: when they see their merchandise returned to them, they will know that the price of the food measured out for them was not taken from them, and that placing the merchandise in the saddlebags was only by Yūsuf's order. And it may be that ”لَعَلَّهم يَرْجِعُونَ“ means: they will return the merchandise, because it is the price of what they had measured out, and because they do not take anything except for its price.

zajjaj:63-63.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَأرْسِلْ مَعَنا أخانا نَكْتَلْ وإنّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ﴾, that is: if you send him with us, we will obtain measure; otherwise we have been denied the measure.

zajjaj:64-64.t: ﴿قالَ هَلْ آمَنُكم عَلَيْهِ إلا كَما أمِنتُكم عَلى أخِيهِ مِن قَبْلُ﴾, that is: you said the same to me about Yūsuf: "Send him with us tomorrow, he will enjoy himself and play, and we will surely guard him"; you guaranteed me Yūsuf's safekeeping, and such is this guarantee of yours in my eyes. ”فاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ حِفْظًا“ — it is also read ﴿حافِظًا﴾. ”حِفْظًا“ is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and ”حافِظًا“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); ”حافِظًا“ may also be a tamyīz.

zajjaj:65-65.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَجَدُوا بِضاعَتَهم رُدَّتْ إلَيْهِمْ﴾; it is also read ”رِدَّتْ“ with kasra of the rāʾ. The origin is ”رُدِدَتْ“; the first dāl was assimilated into the second, and the rāʾ remained with ḍamma. Whoever gives the rāʾ kasra makes its kasra transferred from the dāl, as was done in ”قِيلَ“ and ”بِيعَ“, to indicate that the original vowel of the dāl is kasra. Quṭrub related that in ”ضُرِبَ زَيْدٌ“ (Zayd was struck) one says ”ضُرْبَ زَيْدٌ“ and ”ضِرْبَ زَيْدٌ“ with kasra of the ḍād: he made the rāʾ quiescent and transferred its kasra to the ḍād.
According to this dialect, ”كِبْدٌ“ is permissible for ”كَبِدٌ“.
﴿قالُوا يا أبانا ما نَبْغِي﴾, that is: what do we want? ”ما“ is in the position of the accusative; the meaning is: what [more] would we want, when our merchandise has been returned to us? It may also be that ”ما“ is negation, as if they said: "we do not want anything". ﴿هَذِهِ بِضاعَتُنا رُدَّتْ إلَيْنا ونَمِيرُ أهْلَنا﴾: one says ”مِرْتُهُمْ، أمِيرُهُمْ، مَيْرًا“ when you bring them provisions (mīra). ﴿وَنَـزْدادُ كَيْلَ بَعِيرٍ﴾: because each man used to be measured a camel-load. ﴿ذَلِكَ كَيْلٌ يَسِيرٌ﴾, that is: "that is an easy measure", that is: easy for the one to whom he goes.

zajjaj:66-66.t: ﴿إلا أنْ يُحاطَ بِكُمْ﴾: the position of ”أنْ“ is accusative, and the meaning is: you will surely bring him to me, except on account of being surrounded, that is: you shall not refrain from bringing him except for this. This is called a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). ”إلّا“ here comes in the sense of realising the recompense; you say: "you come only to take the dirhams" and "only that you take the dirhams". The meaning of their being surrounded is that they are prevented from [reaching] him, so they are unable to bring him.

zajjaj:67-67.t: ﴿وَقالَ يا بَنِيَّ لا تَدْخُلُوا مِن بابٍ واحِدٍ وادْخُلُوا مِن أبْوابٍ مُتَفَرِّقَةٍ﴾: he feared the evil eye for them, and the matter of the evil eye is true — and Allah knows best. It has been narrated «from the Prophet ﷺ that he sought protection for al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, saying in his supplication: "I seek protection for you both from every harmful eye"».

zajjaj:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَمّا دَخَلُوا مِن حَيْثُ أمَرَهم أبُوهم ما كانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهم مِنَ اللَّهِ مِن شَيْءٍ إلا حاجَةً في نَفْسِ يَعْقُوبَ قَضاها﴾, that is: except the fear of the evil eye. The interpretation of ”ما كانَ يُغْنِي عَنْهم مِنَ اللَّهِ مِن شَيْءٍ“ is: had it been decreed that it strike them, it would have struck them while separated just as it would strike them together. And it may be: nothing avails against the decree of Allah. ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَذُو عِلْمٍ لِما عَلَّمْناهُ﴾, that is: possessed of knowledge because of Our teaching him. ”حاجَةً“ is accusative as an exception not of the same kind as the first [i.e. a disjoined exception], the meaning being: "but a need in Yaʿqūb's soul which he fulfilled".

zajjaj:69-69.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿آوى إلَيْهِ أخاهُ﴾, that is: he drew his brother close to himself. ﴿فَلا تَبْتَئِسْ﴾, that is: do not grieve and do not be downcast.

zajjaj:70-70.t:
﴿فَلَمّا جَهَّزَهم بِجَهازِهِمْ جَعَلَ السِّقايَةَ في رَحْلِ أخِيهِ ثُمَّ أذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ﴾, that is: an announcer announced. One says: ”آذَنْتُهُ بِالشَّيْءِ، فَهو مُؤْذَنٌ بِهِ“, that is: I informed him; and ”أذَنْتُ“: I announced the thing repeatedly. ﴿أيَّتُها العِيرُ إنَّكم لَسارِقُونَ﴾: the meaning is: "O you, companions of the caravan"; but he said ”أيَّتُها العِيرُ“ meaning "the people of the caravan", as He said: ﴿واسْألِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 82], meaning the people of the town. And he made ”أيُّ“ feminine because he assigned it to "the caravan" (al-ʿīr).
[Translator's note: «أذَنْتُ» is as written; the intensive form is usually «أذَّنْتُ».]

zajjaj:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿قالُوا نَفْقِدُ صُواعَ المَلِكِ﴾; it has been read ”صَواعَ المَلِكِ“ and ”صاعَ المَلِكِ“; Abū Hurayra read ”صاغَ المَلِكِ“; and it has been read ”صَوْغَ المَلِكِ“, with dotted ghayn. ﴿وَلِمَن جاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ﴾, that is: a camel-load of food. ﴿وَأنا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ﴾, that is: guarantor. ”اَلصُّواعُ“ is the ṣāʿ itself, and it is treated as masculine and feminine; likewise ”اَلصّاعُ“ is treated as masculine and feminine. It has come in the exegesis that it was an elongated vessel resembling the makkūk [a measuring vessel], from which the king used to drink, and it is the drinking-cup (al-siqāya). It has been said that it was made of silver plated with gold; it has been said that it was of mis (copper); and it has been said that it resembled a bowl (ṭās).
[Translator's note: The source has «مِن مَسٍّ»; read here as «مِسّ» (copper).]

zajjaj:73-73.t: ﴿قالُوا تاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ ما جِئْنا لِنُفْسِدَ في الأرْضِ﴾: the meaning of ”تاللَّهِ“ is ”واللَّهِ“ (by Allah), except that the oath is not sworn with the tāʾ except with "Allah"; ”تالرَّحْمَنِ“ is not permissible, nor ”تَرَبِّي لَأفْعَلَنَّ“. The tāʾ is a substitute for the wāw, as they said ”تُراثٌ“ for ”وُراثٍ“, and as they said ”يَتَّزِنُ“, whose origin is ”يَوْتَزِنُ“, from ”اَلْوَزْنُ“. They only said ”لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ ما جِئْنا لِنُفْسِدَ في الأرْضِ“ because they would not alight upon a people unjustly, nor graze anyone's crops, and they put muzzles on the mouths of their camels so that they would not meddle with crops. And they said: ﴿وَما كُنّا سارِقِينَ﴾ because, according to what has been narrated, they had returned the merchandise they found in their saddlebags; that is: how can one who returns what he found be a thief?

zajjaj:74-74.t:
﴿قالُوا فَما جَزاؤُهُ إنْ كُنْتُمْ كاذِبِينَ﴾ ﴿قالُوا جَزاؤُهُ مَن وُجِدَ في رَحْلِهِ فَهو جَزاؤُهُ كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي الظّالِمِينَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 75], that is: with the like of this recompense We recompense the wrongdoers. The recompense of the thief among them was that he be enslaved for his theft — he becomes a slave because he stole.
As for the nominative of ”قالُوا جَزاؤُهُ مَن وُجِدَ في رَحْلِهِ“, it is from two angles. One of them is that ”هُوَ جَزاؤُهُ“ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ”مَن وُجِدَ في رَحْلِهِ“ is the khabar (predicate), the meaning being: "the recompense for the theft is the person in whose saddlebag the stolen thing is found"; and His saying ”فَهُوَ جَزاؤُهُ“ is an addition for clarity, as you say: "The recompense of the thief is the cutting [of the hand]; that is his recompense; this is his recompense" — as an addition for clarity.
[Translator's note: The source writes «أنَّ "هُوَ جَزاؤُهُ"، اِبْتِداءٌ»; from the analysis that follows, the mubtadaʾ meant is evidently the first «جَزاؤُهُ». Translated as written.]
And it may be that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with ”مَن وُجِدَ في رَحْلِهِ فَهو جَزاؤُهُ“ — this clause — being the khabar of "the recompense", the pronoun-link (ʿāʾid) to it from the clause being ”جَزاؤُهُ“ that comes after His saying ”فَهُوَ“; as if it were said: "They said: its recompense — the one in whose saddlebag it is found, he is it", that is: "he is the recompense". But the overt [noun] was better here, so that no ambiguity would occur in the speech, and so that it would not be imagined that ”هُوَ“, if it recurred a second time, did not refer back to "the recompense". When the Arabs give emphatic prominence to the matter of a thing, they make the link to it a repetition of its very wording. All the grammarians recited:
؎لا أرى المَوْتَ يَسْبِقُ المَوْتَ شَيْءٌ نَغَّصَ المَوْتُ ذا الغِنى والفَقِيرا
(I see that nothing outstrips death; death has troubled both the rich and the poor.)
and he did not say: "I see that nothing outstrips it".

zajjaj:76-76.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَخْرَجَها مِن وِعاءِ أخِيهِ﴾: the feminine refers back to the drinking-cup (al-siqāya); and it may be that he treated al-ṣuwāʿ as feminine. ﴿كَذَلِكَ كِدْنا لِيُوسُفَ ما كانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أخاهُ في دِينِ المَلِكِ﴾, that is: in the custom of the king and what the king follows as law, because in the king's law the thief was fined twice what he stole.
Among the family of Yaʿqūb, and in their way, the thief became a slave, enslaved by the owner of the stolen thing. ﴿إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: the position of ”أنْ“ is accusative; when the bāʾ dropped out, the verb reached it directly and put it in the accusative. The meaning is: "he could not take his brother under the king's law except by the will of Allah". ”نَرْفَعُ دَرَجاتِ مَن نَشاءُ“ is by annexing "degrees" to ”مَن“; ”دَرَجاتٍ“ with tanwīn is also permissible, with ”مَن“ in the position of the accusative, the meaning being: "We raise whom We will by degrees".
The nominative ”دَرَجاتٌ مَن نَشاءُ“ is also permissible and is good, but I do not know that it has been narrated, so do not ever read it unless a sound narration of it is established. ﴿وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾: it was said in the exegesis: "above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing", until knowledge ends with Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:77-77.t:
﴿قالُوا إنْ يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أخٌ لَهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾: they mean Yūsuf. It is narrated that in his childhood he took an image made of gold, of the things with which some of those opposed to the people of the religion of Islam used to worship; and his taking it was by way of disapproval, so that such a thing would not be venerated. ﴿فَأسَرَّها يُوسُفُ في نَفْسِهِ ولَمْ يُبْدِها لَهُمْ﴾, that is: he did not show it to them. ﴿قالَ أنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكانًا﴾
This is a pronoun used on condition of later explanation (iḍmār ʿalā sharīṭat al-tafsīr), because His saying ”قالَ أنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكانًا“ is a badal (substitute) for the ”ها“ in His saying ﴿فَأسَرَّها﴾. The meaning is: "So Yūsuf kept secret within himself his saying: ﴿أنْتُمْ شَرٌّ مَكانًا﴾". The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: you are in a worse position in theft, in truth, because you stole your brother from your father. ﴿واللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِما تَصِفُونَ﴾, that is: "Allah knows best whether a brother of his stole or not".

zajjaj:78-78.t: ﴿قالُوا يا أيُّها العَزِيزُ﴾: ”اَلْعَزِيزُ“ is the king. ﴿إنَّ لَهُ أبًا شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا﴾: ”شَيْخًا“ is a naʿt (adjective) of ”أبًا“; ”أبًا“ is accusative by ”إنَّ“; and ”كَبِيرًا“ is a naʿt of ”شَيْخًا“. ﴿فَخُذْ أحَدَنا مَكانَهُ إنّا نَراكَ مِنَ المُحْسِنِينَ﴾, that is: of those who act generously and do not deal strictly by the letter in what is due, because he had given them the food and given them its price by returning the merchandise to them; so they asked him to act generously.

zajjaj:79-79.t: ﴿قالَ مَعاذَ اللَّهِ أنْ نَأْخُذَ إلا مَن وجَدْنا مَتاعَنا عِنْدَهُ﴾: ”مَعاذَ اللَّهِ“ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. mafʿūl muṭlaq], the meaning being: "I seek refuge in Allah with a seeking of refuge". The position of ”أنْ“ is accusative; the meaning is: I seek refuge in Allah from taking anyone except the one with whom we found our property; when ”مِن“ dropped out, the verb reached it directly and put it in the accusative. ﴿إنّا إذًا لَظالِمُونَ﴾, that is: if we took someone else, we would be wrongdoers.

zajjaj:80-80.t:
﴿فَلَمّا اسْتَيْأسُوا مِنهُ خَلَصُوا نَجِيًّا﴾: the meaning is: they withdrew conferring privately, that is: they withdrew as people conferring privately about what they would do in going to their father without their brother with them. ”نَجِيٌّ“ is a singular word with a plural meaning; likewise ﴿وَإذْ هم نَجْوى﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 47]. One may say ”قَوْمٌ نَجِيٌّ“, ”قَوْمٌ نَجْوى“ and ”قَوْمٌ أنْجِيَةٌ“. The poet said:
؎إنِّي إذا ما القَوْمُ صارُوا أنْجِيَةْ
؎واخْتَلَفَ القَوْلُ اخْتِلافَ الأرْشِيَةْ
؎هُناكَ أوْصِينِي ولا تُوصِي بِيَهْ
(When the people become groups conferring in secret, and talk goes back and forth like well-ropes, then entrust [matters] to me, and do not entrust me [to others].)
The meaning of ”خَلَصُوا“ is: they went apart, their brother not being with them.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمِن قَبْلُ ما فَرَّطْتُمْ في يُوسُفَ﴾: the best of the ways is that ”ما“ is redundant (laghw), so the meaning is: "and before, you failed in your duty concerning Yūsuf". It may be that ”ما“ is in the position of the nominative, so the meaning is: "and before [was] your failure concerning Yūsuf", that is: "your failure concerning Yūsuf occurred". And it may be that ”ما“ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined (nasaq) to ”أنَّ“, the meaning being: "Do you not know that your father … and know your failure concerning Yūsuf?" ﴿فَلَنْ أبْرَحَ الأرْضَ حَتّى يَأْذَنَ لِي أبِي﴾, that is: I will not leave the land of Egypt — otherwise all people are on the earth. ﴿أوْ يَحْكُمَ اللَّهُ لِي﴾ is conjoined to ”حَتّى يَأْذَنَ“; and it may be that ”أوْ“ is as the answer to ”لَنْ“, the meaning being: "I will not leave the land until Allah judges for me".

zajjaj:81-81.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ ابْنَكَ سَرَقَ﴾; ”سُرِّقَ“ is also permissible, though ”سَرَقَ“ is firmer in the reading. ”سُرِّقَ“ may be of two kinds: ”سُرِّقَ“: it became known that he stole; and ”سُرِّقَ“: he was accused of theft.

zajjaj:83-83.t: ﴿قالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكم أنْفُسُكُمْ﴾, that is: your souls have made [it] seem fair to you, and your souls have endeared [it] to you. ﴿فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ﴾: the meaning is "my affair is beautiful patience", or "my patience is beautiful patience". We have explained this earlier in the sūra.

zajjaj:84-84.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أسَفى عَلى يُوسُفَ﴾: its meaning is "O my grief!". The origin is ”يا أسَفِي“, except that the yāʾ of annexation may be replaced by alif because of the lightness of the alif and the fatḥa. ﴿فَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ﴾, that is: grief-stricken.

zajjaj:85-85.t:
﴿قالُوا تاللَّهِ تَفْتَأُ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ﴾: the meaning of ”تاللَّهِ“ is ”واللَّهِ“ (by Allah), and ”لا“ is implied (muḍmara); the meaning is: "By Allah, you will not cease remembering Yūsuf", that is: "you will continue remembering Yūsuf". ﴿حَتّى تَكُونَ حَرَضًا﴾: ”اَلْحَرَضُ“ is one corrupted in his body, that is: "until you are wasting and sick"; and ”اَلْحَرَضُ“ is one corrupted in his character. Their saying "I incited (ḥarraḍtu) so-and-so against so-and-so" is to be interpreted as: I corrupted him against him.
The implying of ”لا“ in His saying ”تاللَّهِ تَفْتَأُ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ“ is permissible only because in the oath ”تاللَّهِ تَفْعَلُ“ is not permissible unless you say ”لَتَفْعَلَنَّ“ or ”لا تَفْعَلْ“.
[Translator's note: «لا تَفْعَلْ» is as written (with jussive sukūn); in an oath the negated form is normally «لا تَفْعَلُ».]
Swearing oaths is not permissible for people except by Allah, Mighty and Majestic. A man may not swear by his father, nor ought he to swear by the prophets; he should swear only by Allah. It is narrated «from the Prophet, upon him be peace, that he said to ʿUmar: "Do not swear by your fathers; whoever swears, let him swear by Allah"».
If someone says: What then is the sense of the oath in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His saying: ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا يَغْشى﴾ [al-Layl: 1], ﴿والسَّماءِ ذاتِ البُرُوجِ﴾ [al-Burūj: 1], ﴿والتِّينِ والزَّيْتُونِ﴾ [al-Tīn: 1], and the like of these things which Allah, Majestic is His majesty, mentioned in His Book? There are several ways concerning them, all of which the Basrans mentioned. They said: it may be that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, swore by them because in all of them there is evidence pointing to Him and clear signs. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إنَّ في خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ واخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 164] — to the end of the verse.
And He said: ﴿وَفِي خَلْقِكم وما يَبُثُّ مِن دابَّةٍ آياتٌ﴾ [al-Jāthiya: 4]. So the oath by these indicates the greatness of Allah. Quṭrub said: it may be that its meaning is "by the Lord of the sun and its morning brightness", "by the Lord of the fig and the olive", as He said: ﴿والسَّماءِ ذاتِ البُرُوجِ﴾ [al-Burūj: 1], and He said: ﴿والأرْضِ وما طَحاها﴾ [al-Shams: 6],
and He said: ﴿فَوَرَبِّ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ إنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 23]. They also said: it may be "by the creation of the heavens and the earth", "by the creation of the fig and the olive". And they said: it may be that, since the meaning of an oath is the meaning of affirmation, and these things by which Allah swore are all real, likewise what He swore about is real; so the meaning is: "Just as the fig and the olive are real, We have certainly created man in the best stature". The best of these views is the one we began with first.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَجِئْنا بِبِضاعَةٍ مُزْجاةٍ﴾: they said ”مُزْجاةٍ“ means scanty. They said: they had brought Bedouin goods such as wool, clarified butter and the like, of what Bedouins sell. It has been said that the merchandise was of a kind whose like does not sell for food, because Bedouin goods were like that — low-grade wealth lay beneath them. Its interpretation in the language is that ”اَلتَّزْجِيَةُ“ is the small thing with which one gets by. You say: "so-and-so yuzajjī his living", that is: he gets by with little and makes do with it. So the meaning on this view is: "We have brought merchandise with which one can only get by", that is: "subsist", "not of that with which one lives in ease". The poet said:
؎اَلْواهِبُ المِائَةَ الهِجانَ وعَبْدَها عُوذُوا تُزَجِّي خَلْفَها أطْفالَها
(The giver of a hundred pure-white camels with their herdsman, recently foaled, driving their young along behind them.)
that is: driving their young along.

zajjaj:90-90.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قالُوا أإنَّكَ لأنْتَ يُوسُفُ﴾: there are four ways in it: combining the two hamzas, ”قالُوا أئِنَّكَ“, pronouncing both fully; ”أيِنَّكَ“ is permissible, making the second between yāʾ and hamza; it has been read ”آئِنَّكَ“ [i.e. the question hamza] onto ”إنَّكَ“, separating the two hamzas with an alif because of the meeting of the two hamzas. The poet said:
؎أيا ظَبْيَةَ الوَعْساءِ بَيْنَ جَلاجِلٍ وبَيْنَ النَّقا آأنْتِ أمْ أُمُّ سالِمِ
(O gazelle of the sandy ground between Jalājil and the dune — is it you, or Umm Sālim?)
And ”قالُوا إنَّكَ لَأنْتَ“ in the form of a statement is permissible.

zajjaj:92-92.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ اليَوْمَ﴾, that is: no spoiling [of you] is upon you.

zajjaj:94-94.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَوْلا أنْ تُفَنِّدُونِ﴾: its meaning is: were it not that you would call me ignorant; and ”تُسَفِّهُونِ“ (call me foolish) is also narrated.

zajjaj:97-97.t:
His saying: ﴿إنّا كُنّا خاطِئِينَ﴾: one says ”قَدْ خَطِئَ، يَخْطَأُ، خَطَأً، وخَطْأً“ (he sinned / erred intentionally) and ”أخْطَأ، يُخْطِئُ، إخْطاءً“ (he erred). Imruʾ al-Qays said:
؎يا لَهْفَ هِنْدٍ إذْ خَطِئْنَ كاهِلًا اَلْقاتِلِينَ المَلِكَ الحُلاحِلا
(Alas for Hind, when they [the horses] missed Kāhil, the slayers of the noble, lordly king!)

zajjaj:98-98.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿سَوْفَ أسْتَغْفِرُ لَكم رَبِّي﴾: Yaʿqūb said that intending to seek forgiveness for them at the time of the onset of the pre-dawn (saḥar), the time that is for the answering of supplication — not that he was stingy with seeking forgiveness. That is more in keeping with the character of the prophets, I mean exerting oneself in seeking forgiveness and deliberately choosing the time of answering.

zajjaj:99-99.t: ﴿آوى إلَيْهِ أبَوَيْهِ﴾, that is: he drew his parents close to himself.

zajjaj:100-100.t: ﴿وَرَفَعَ أبَوَيْهِ عَلى العَرْشِ﴾: ”اَلْعَرْشُ“ is the throne-couch (al-sarīr). ﴿وَخَرُّوا لَهُ سُجَّدًا﴾: it was part of the custom of honouring at that time to prostrate to the one honoured. And it has been said: ”وَخَرُّوا لَهُ سُجَّدًا“ means "and they fell down [prostrating] to Allah".

zajjaj:101-101.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ المُلْكِ وعَلَّمْتَنِي مِن تَأْوِيلِ الأحادِيثِ﴾: there are two views on it — I mean on the entry of ”مِن“. It may be that he meant: You have taught me some of the interpretation and given me some of the kingship; and it may be that ”مِن“ enters to distinguish this genus from all other genera, so the meaning is: "My Lord, You have given me kingship and taught me the interpretation of accounts", like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿تُؤْتِي المُلْكَ مَن تَشاءُ وتَنْـزِعُ المُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشاءُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 26]. [This] indicates that ”مِن“ here is only for specifying the genus (tabyīn al-jins). Like it is His saying: ﴿فاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأوْثانِ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 30]: they were not commanded to avoid some of the idols; rather the meaning is: "avoid the filth which is the idols".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فاطِرَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ is accusative in two ways. One of them is as an attribute, by His saying ”رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ المُلْكِ“, the meaning being "O my Lord, You have given me": this is an annexed vocative in the position of the accusative, and ”فاطِرَ السَّمَواتِ والأرْضِ“ is an attribute of the first. And it may be accusative as a second vocative, so the meaning is: "O Originator of the heavens and the earth". ﴿أنْتَ ولِيِّي﴾
﴿وَألْحِقْنِي بِالصّالِحِينَ﴾, that is: join me to their ranks of Your mercy and Your forgiveness.

zajjaj:102-102.t:
﴿ذَلِكَ مِن أنْباءِ الغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إلَيْكَ﴾: this is an address to the Prophet, upon him be peace. The meaning is: "What We have related to you of the matter of Yūsuf and his brothers is of the reports that were hidden from you". So it was sent down upon him as a proof establishing his prophethood, as a warning, and as an easing by detailing the stories of past nations. The position of ”ذَلِكَ“ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being ”مِن أنْباءِ الغَيْبِ“, and ”نُوحِيهِ إلَيْكَ“ a second khabar. If you wish, you may make ”نُوحِيهِ“ the khabar and put ”ذَلِكَ“ in the place of ”اَلَّذِي“ (which), the meaning being: "That which is of the reports of the unseen, We reveal it to you".
[Translator's note: The source's final paraphrase reads «اَلَّذِي مِن أنْباءِ الغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إلَيْكَ ذَلِكَ», with «ذَلِكَ» placed at the end; rendered by sense.]

zajjaj:103-103.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما أكْثَرُ النّاسِ ولَوْ حَرَصْتَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: its meaning is: "Most people are not believers, even if you were eager to guide them, because you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills".

zajjaj:104-104.t: ﴿وَما تَسْألُهم عَلَيْهِ مِن أجْرٍ﴾, that is: "You do not ask them any wage for the Qur'an, its recitation and your guiding them". ﴿إنْ هو إلا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾, that is: "It is only a reminder to them of what is their well-being, their deliverance from the Fire, their entering Paradise, their being warned and given good tidings; all well-being is in it".

zajjaj:105-105.t:
﴿وَكَأيِّنْ مِن آيَةٍ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, that is: of a sign and an indication that points them to the oneness of Allah: of the matter of the sky — that it is without pillars and does not fall upon the earth, and that it contains the courses of the sun and the moon that it contains; in it is the greatest proof and evidence that the One who created it is one, and that it has a Creator — and likewise in what is witnessed on the earth, of its plants, its seas and its mountains. ﴿وَهم عَنْها مُعْرِضُونَ﴾, that is: they do not reflect on what points them to the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and the proof that they do not reflect on that by which they would infer
[Translator's note: The source text breaks off here mid-sentence.]

zajjaj:106-106.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما يُؤْمِنُ أكْثَرُهم بِاللَّهِ إلا وهم مُشْرِكُونَ﴾, that is: if they acknowledged that Allah is their Creator and the Creator of the heavens and the earth, they associated idols in His worship, and they associated [things] other than idols.

zajjaj:107-107.t: ﴿أفَأمِنُوا أنْ تَأْتِيَهم غاشِيَةٌ مِن عَذابِ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: that there come to them punishment that overpowers them. ﴿أوْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ السّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً﴾, that is: suddenly. ”بَغْتَةً“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). You say: "I met him baghtatan and fajʾatan", and its meaning is: from where I did not expect to meet him.

zajjaj:109-109.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَدارُ الآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾, and in more than one place: ﴿وَلَلدّارُ الآخِرَةُ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 32]. Whoever says ”اَلدّارُ الآخِرَةُ“, then ”اَلْآخِرَةُ“ is a naʿt (adjective) of "the abode", because all creatures have two abodes: the abode in which they were created, which is this world, and the last abode, in which they are brought back as a new creation. Whoever says ”دارُ الآخِرَةِ“, it is as if he said "the abode of the last life", because people have two lives: the life of this world and the life of the Hereafter. The like of this in speech is ”اَلصَّلاةُ الأُولى“ and ”صَلاةُ الأُولى“: whoever says ”اَلصَّلاةُ الأُولى“ makes ”اَلْأُولى“ a naʿt of the prayer, and whoever says ”صَلاةُ الأُولى“ means "the prayer of the first obligatory [prayer]" and "the first hour".

zajjaj:110-110.t:
﴿حَتّى إذا اسْتَيْئَسَ الرُّسُلُ وظَنُّوا أنَّهم قَدْ كُذِبُوا﴾: it has been read ”كُذِبُوا“ and ”كُذِّبُوا“, with the light and the doubled [dhāl], and it has been read ”وَكَذَبُوا“. As for whoever reads ”وَظَنُّوا أنَّهم قَدْ كُذِّبُوا“ with the doubling, the meaning is: "until, when the messengers despaired of their people believing them, Our help came to them". And whoever reads ”قَدْ كُذِبُوا“ with the light [dhāl], the meaning is: "and their people thought that they [the messengers] had been told a lie in what they were promised", because the messengers would not think that.
Some said: "and they thought that they had been failed (ukhlifū)", that is, the messengers thought so; that is far-fetched as a description of the messengers. It is narrated from ʿĀʾisha that the Prophet ﷺ was never promised anything in which he was failed, and in the report: "Allah forbid that the messengers should think this of their Lord". And the meaning of ”وَظَنُّوا أنَّهم قَدْ [كَذَبُوا]“ is: "their people also thought that they [the messengers] had lied".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَنُجِّيَ مَن نَشاءُ﴾: it has been read ”فَنُنَجِّي“ and ”فَنُنْجِيَ“; it has been read ”فَنَجا مَن نَشاءُ“; and ʿĀṣim read ”فَنُجِّيَ مَن نَشاءُ“ with fatḥa of the yāʾ. As for whoever reads ”فَنُنْجِيَ“, it is as future, the nūn being the nūn of the imperfect — I mean the first nūn. Whoever reads ”فَنُجِّي“ with sukūn of the yāʾ elided the second nūn because of the meeting of the two nūns, as you say: "you tabayyanu this matter", meaning tatabayyanu, eliding because of the meeting of two tāʾs.
Whoever reads ”فَنَجا مَن نَشاءُ“ conjoins it to His saying "Our help came to them, so whom We willed was saved", in the form of the past verb. Whoever reads ”فَنُجِّيَ مَن نَشاءُ“ has it in the past sense, as a verb whose agent is not named [i.e. passive], and the position of ”مَن“ is nominative; it is known from the meaning that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saved them.
